articles.title: ‘It’s huge’: Nike deal breaks new ground for London City Lionesses
articles.summary: Sponsorship agreement is largest in women’s game. Exceeds some men’s Premier League clubs’ shirt deals. The Women’s Super League club London City Lionesses’ new front-of-shirt sponsorship deal with Nike is the largest in the women’s game, according to their American owner, Michele Kang.
body: The length and value of the deal has not been disclosed but sources close to the WSL club are hailing it as a gamechanging moment and Kang claims that it even exceeds some men’s Premier League clubs’ shirt deals.

London City, who host Manchester United on Friday in the opening game of the new WSL campaign, are about to embark on only their second top-flight season, but this summer they have shocked the sport by signing a flurry of some of the biggest names in women’s football, including the former Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas, the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps and Putellas’ Spain and Barcelona teammate, Mapi León.

It has been reported that the largest current front-of-shirt sponsorship deal for a women’s football team is an approximately $4m per year agreement reached by the new NWSL franchise in Atlanta – who will begin competing in 2028, but Kang told BBC Sport: “I can absolutely confirm that this is the largest women-only front-of-shirt deal. It is higher than the Atlanta number.

articles.title: Bradford end losing run with win over Castleford
articles.summary: Bradford Bulls end a seven-match losing streak with victory over troubled Castleford Tigers in the struggle to avoid the Super League wooden spoon.
body: Bradford Bulls ended their run of seven straight defeats and deepened the gloom surrounding Castleford Tigers at Odsal Stadium.

The return of three experienced forwards gave Bradford a major boost as they dominated from the start against Castleford, who are without a head coach and have now lost six of their past seven games since beating league leaders Leeds Rhinos in July.

Bradford took control by half-time with tries from Riley Dean, Connor Wynne, Caleb Aekins, Dan Russell and Waqa Blake as scrum-half Chris Atkin ran the show with Louis Senior's try the only points for Castleford in the first half.

They improved in the second half with two tries from Krystian Mapapalangi and one from Alex Mellor, but Ebon Scurr's try 12 minutes after the interval was enough to keep Castleford at arm's length and move Bradford level on points with York Knights, Huddersfield Giants and Hull FC with one game to play.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership: McPake’s solo pearler seals Hearts’ cruise past 10-man Hibs
articles.summary: Camilo Durán inspires Celtic’s 3-0 win against Aberdeen. Falkirk 1-2 Rangers; Kilmarnock 0-1 St Mirren. Wouter Vrancken enjoyed a memorable first Edinburgh derby in charge of Hearts as his rampant side cruised to a deserved 3-1 victory over 10-man Hibernian at Easter Road.
body: James Wilson and Laurent Mendy had the visitors two goals up at half-time before Hibs ralled early in the second half and pulled one back through substitute Adam Mayor.

Their hopes of a fightback were dashed, however, when Josh McPake – in front of the watching Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli – scored a brilliant third for Hearts shortly after Hibs substitute Jack Iredale was sent off. McPake’s superb solo run was capped with a finish that deflected in off Grant Hanley.
It was a seventh successive match unbeaten in all competitions for Hearts, who have recovered impressively after losing each of their first four matches under the ultra-cavalier Vrancken.
The Celtic striker Camilo Durán inspired the Scottish champions’ 3-0 win over Aberdeen, while Rangers snatched a 2-1 victory against Falkirk on Wednesday.

articles.title: GB's Dart struggles with illness in second-round exit
articles.summary: Britain's Harriet Dart says she felt "under the weather" as she struggles in the heat during her second-round loss to Marie Bouzkova at the US Open.
body: Dart struggled for rhythm in a 6-2 6-2 defeat by Czech 25th seed Bouzkova as temperatures reached around 30C in New York.
Dart's defeat means Fran Jones is the last remaining Briton in either singles draw at Flushing Meadows.
Dart draped ice towels around her neck and used cold-air hoses at the changeovers against Bouzkova as she attempted to cool down.
"I have been a bit under the weather. It is what it is, sadly," Dart, 30, said.

articles.title: We want Fury v Joshua at Wembley - London mayor
articles.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in touch.
body: BBC Sport understands Saudi organisers Sela have contacted the mayor's office in recent weeks about bringing the long-awaited contest to the national stadium.

However, with organisers and broadcaster Netflix understood to favour New York's Madison Square Garden for a November bout, sources close to the discussions say talks over a London venue have not progressed, with no detailed talks over dates or timings.
"A message to the promoters - we want to host it in London. Talk to us, we're really keen to have it," Khan told BBC Sport on Thursday.
Wembley Stadium's usual curfew is 23:00, although Khan has previously indicated he would support efforts to bring the fight to London.

articles.title: Houston Astros take control early, cruise to easy victory to take 4-game series vs. White Sox
articles.summary: Houston continued its recent resurgence, taking three of four against a fellow division leader thanks to fast offensive start and Hunter Brown's quality start.
body: For a day, the Houston Astros enjoyed the elements of a formulaic win. An early lead. A quality start. A relatively rested bullpen.

With them, they sailed to a 6-2 victory over the Chicago White Sox and secured their first series win at Daikin Park in more than a month. Houston had lost its past four home series. It took three of four from the American League Central leaders and won the teams' season series, 5-2.

No division in baseball is more woeful than the AL West, though the AL Central is close. Still, the Astros extended their AL West lead to 2 ½ games, pending the Rangers' result later Thursday, and returned to their high-water mark at three games over.500 with 21 to play in their season.

The Astros have won seven of 10 games since a dismal homestand and the dismissal of their general manager, an upturn at an opportune time. Their next three series are also against contending teams, starting with the Arizona Diamondbacks ' arrival this weekend.

articles.title: ‘Otherwise won’t win’ – Jose Mourinho issues stark Real Madrid warning ahead of Betis clash
articles.summary: Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has issued a strong warning to his players as the team braces to face Real Betis on Friday at Estadio de La Cartuja. ‘The Special One’, who returned for his second stint at Madrid this year in June, is leaving no stone unturned to ensure a strong 2026 La Liga season…
body: As the team braces for Friday’s challenge, Mourinho said in the press conference that it has to be a great Real Madrid otherwise the team won’t win. He further lauded the Betis team while acknowledging Madrid’s recent good results. He also warned his team that winning at Betis’ backyard won’t be easy.

“It has to be a great Real Madrid, otherwise, they won’t win,” Mourinho said. “Betis, as you say, is a very good team. Real Madrid’s recent results there speak for themselves. It is difficult to win there. To win, you have to be at your very best level. There is no other way,” he concluded.

In the three wins that Madrid have secured this season so far, the team has scored 10 goals while conceding two, giving them a goal difference of +8 and placing them second in the standings behind Barcelona.

With everything set, Madridistas will be looking forward to players like Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham, who have been terrific so far this season, bringing their A-game to Estadio de La Cartuja so that their unbeaten run continues.

articles.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino
articles.summary: FIFA has accused European football’s governing body of launching a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino in a challenge to legal action over the aborted attempt to sell part of the World Cup to private investors.
body: UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts.

UEFA has filed legal cases in American courts seeking evidence relating to the controversial venture and warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland where FIFA has its headquarters.

FIFA has now filed a response in a New York court, saying: "While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership."
UEFA is trying to oust Mr Infantino from power with a resignation or in the FIFA presidential election in March.

articles.title: Bill Belichick’s general manager resigns amidst investigation
articles.summary: Back in July, North Carolina Tar Heels football general manager Michael Lombardi was placed on paid leave in the wake of an internal investigation. Now, he has officially resigned from his post.
body: Less than a week after North Carolina officially began its season with a win over TCU, they will now be without their general manager going forward.

Lombardi, who has worked with Bill Belichick across intermittent stints spanning nearly 40 years, beginning with the Cleveland Browns in the late 1980s, was placed on administrative leave while the university launched an internal investigation.

“The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill has placed Michael Lombardi, general manager for the Carolina football program, on paid administrative leave, effective immediately,” UNC said via statement. “As is standard procedure with personnel matters, leadership, staff, and student-athletes are prohibited from addressing this topic further, and has no reflection on the merits.”

ESPN’s Pete Thamel followed up with a report that the decision to place Lombardi, who is in the second year of a three-year deal that pays a base rate of $1.5 million per year, on leave stemmed from a complaint filed by a former UNC front office employee.

articles.title: All right for Wong as England seamer 'keeps things simple'
articles.summary: England bowler Issy Wong likes delving into her box of tricks - off the field when she completes Rubik's Cubes in next to no time and on it as she tries to get batters out.
body: But the seamer was rewarded for simplicity on Thursday as a five-wicket haul - her first in international cricket - helped her side wrap up an one-day international series win over Ireland.
Prioritising the wobble-seam delivery that angled in to the right handers, Wong bowled opposition captain Gaby Lewis through the gate for her first strike of the day.
Her relentless targeting of the stumps also saw her clean up Leah Paul off an inside edge, while her three other victims, including top-scorer Amy Hunter, were caught.
Wong had struggled for accuracy during England's victory in the series opener at Leicester on Tuesday, conceding four wides in a row as she curled balls too far past off stump.
